title: The Powder River, June 1866: an Oglala camp
summary: Early summer in the Powder River country, the best hunting ground the Lakota have left. The treaty council is at Fort Laramie, Red Cloud says no road will cross this land, and soldiers are on their way north anyway. Be one of its people, or make your own.

playerSlot.summary: You make your own person of an Oglala camp on the Tongue River in the Powder River country, in the summer the soldiers came to build their road.

roles.label: Hunter
roles.desc: Rides after buffalo and elk; the camp eats what the hunters bring.

roles.label: Young warrior
roles.desc: Guards the camp and the horse herd, and wants to be counted among the men.

roles.label: Healer
roles.desc: Knows the plants and the ways of healing.

roles.label: Quillworker or hide worker
roles.desc: Makes the lodges, clothes and robes the camp lives in, and trades them.

roles.label: Go-between
roles.desc: Speaks the traders' languages and goes to the posts for the camp.

peoples.label: Of another Lakota people
peoples.desc: Miniconjou, Brulé, Hunkpapa or another, living in this camp.

peoples.label: Northern Cheyenne
peoples.desc: Of the Lakota's Cheyenne allies, with family here.

clocks.name: Word from the council
clocks.fireText: A rider comes in from Fort Laramie with the news of the council, and the whole camp gathers to hear what was said.

opening:
Morning on the Tongue River. The lodges stand in a wide circle among the cottonwoods, meat drying on the racks, the horse herd grazing fat on the summer grass. It is a good camp, and everyone knows it may be the last good summer.

Bear Shield and the other old men went south to the council at Fort Laramie and came back only yesterday, tired and quiet. Louis Brasseur rode in with them, and has not yet said what the soldiers' chiefs want.

Kills in Winter sits at your fire, checking the action of his carbine, and does not look up. "Bear Shield says they will talk again," he says. "Talk. While their soldiers walk up our road."
